summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with a symptomatic urinary tract infection caused by multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, complicated by acute delirium and myoclonic jerks. He was started on cefepime, which was later changed to imipenem based on culture results. His mental status improved rapidly with appropriate antibiotic therapy. A groin rash was diagnosed as candidiasis and treated with topical ketoconazole. His foley catheter was exchanged to reduce infection risk. He completed a course of IV antibiotics and was discharged to extended care for 10 days of daily ertapenem injections. His chronic conditions, including diastolic heart failure, benign prostatic hypertrophy, and a right renal mass, remained stable. Blood cultures remained negative, and imaging showed no new acute findings.
